exposure: behavioral information (daily meal fixed time, average daily eating habits)
cohort: The study included 1282 medical students, aged 16 to 27 years, from a university in Inner Mongolia, China.
finding: The study revealed a high prevalence of anxiety (10.36%) and depression (24.43%) among medical students, with birthplace and whether daily meals were at a fixed time significantly associated with both conditions.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as an independent risk factor for depressive disorder among the medical students.
